prs.title: Expose KarrasUnet Fourier conditioning to continuous diffusion wrappers
prs.body:
## Problem

The exported KarrasUnet cannot be passed to ElucidatedDiffusion, ContinuousTimeGaussianDiffusion or VParamContinuousTimeGaussianDiffusion: their constructors access `random_or_learned_sinusoidal_cond`, which this model does not define. Construction raises AttributeError before any training or sampling. The model already uses fixed random Fourier time embeddings.

## Change

Declare that existing Fourier-conditioning capability on the 2D KarrasUnet. This adds metadata only; it does not change its parameters, state-dictionary entries, forward calculation or the diffusion wrappers' validation. Add an unconditional KarrasUnet/ElucidatedDiffusion usage example.

## Validation

- 13 native tests: original source **10 failed, 3 passed**; patched source **13 passed**.
- All three wrappers train real grayscale and RGB Karras models for two Adam updates. Losses and gradients stay finite, input/time-projection weights receive nonzero gradients, and random Fourier frequencies remain frozen.
- Native Heun, DPM++, continuous noise-prediction and continuous velocity-prediction sampling return finite images of the expected shape and range.
- ElucidatedDiffusion also trains and samples with self-conditioning enabled.
- The two continuous wrappers still reject unsupported self-conditioning, and all three wrappers still reject standard non-Fourier Unets.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. This enables the tested unconditional 2D interface; it does not add class-label routing or 1D/3D wrapper support. No GPU run, full training or image-quality benchmark was performed.

prs.title: Evaluate learned noise-schedule endpoints once per call
prs.body:
## Problem

The learned noise schedule evaluates its monotonic network at zero and one separately for every requested time. Those endpoint inputs are identical across the batch, but both network activations and their backward work scale with its size.

## Change

Evaluate each endpoint once using a scalar created from the input tensor, then broadcast the endpoint values in the existing normalization. Keep dtype/device, endpoint gradients, the gradient-fraction setting and the per-call recalculation after optimizer updates. The network contains no batch-dependent or random layers.

## Validation

- **34 native tests pass both before and after** this performance change.
- Float32/float64 values, input derivatives and every parameter derivative match a full-batch endpoint reference for scalar, singleton, vector, matrix and empty inputs, with gradient fractions 0, 0.3 and 1.
- A real Unet with ContinuousTimeGaussianDiffusion and a learned schedule performs two SGD updates against a full-batch reference; losses, all gradients and final parameters agree.
- Endpoint values and monotonicity remain covered.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Local CPU measurements use the native schedule forward and backward, hidden width 1024, float32, two threads, fixed parameters and three fresh processes for every input size and implementation. Each process runs three warmups followed by 20 measurements (eight for batch 4096). The table reports the median of the process medians.

| Batch size | Original forward/backward | New forward/backward | Original additional peak RSS | New additional peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.391 ms | 0.397 ms | 8.391 MiB | 8.391 MiB |
| 256 | 3.315 ms | 1.459 ms | 17.328 MiB | 13.582 MiB |
| 4096 | 41.985 ms | 23.283 ms | 136.824 MiB | 72.641 MiB |

These are schedule-only CPU timings and process high-water memory increases after constructing the inputs/model. They exclude the Unet and optimizer, and the singleton case did not improve. No GPU or end-to-end training speedup is claimed. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu.

prs.title: Allow scalar block counts in KarrasUnet3D without downsampling
prs.body:
## Problem

`KarrasUnet3D(num_downsamples=0, num_blocks_per_stage=1)` cannot construct a model. The scalar block count is expanded to an empty tuple, then unpacked to obtain its first entry. An explicit one-element tuple works, so the scalar and tuple forms disagree for an architecture that keeps the original resolution.

## Change

Expand a scalar block count to `num_downsamples + 1` stages, including the initial stage. Positive downsampling counts produce the same stage counts as before, and the legacy short-tuple expansion remains unchanged.

## Validation

- 19 native tests: original source **4 failed, 15 passed**; patched source **19 passed**.
- Real 3D Unets with 0/1/2 downsampling stages, 1/2 blocks and self-conditioning on/off are compared with equivalent explicit full-stage tuples.
- Initial state dictionaries, outputs, input gradients, all trainable parameter gradients and final weights match exactly through two Adam updates. The input weights change and gradients stay finite.
- Short tuples retain their existing expansion for joint, spatial-only and temporal-only downsampling configurations.
- Invalid stage lengths and nonpositive block counts remain rejected.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. No GPU execution, full training or video-quality benchmark was run.

prs.title: Enable paired UViT image transforms with the configured channels
prs.body:
## Problem

Providing both `init_img_transform` and `final_img_itransform` to UViT raises a TypeError before the model is initialized: `torch.Size` is called with four positional arguments instead of one dimension sequence. The probe also hardcodes one channel, so channel-aware RGB transforms cannot be validated against the configured input.

## Change

Construct the probe shape from one tuple containing the batch size, configured channel count and existing spatial dimensions. Preserve the inverse-transform shape check and the existing forward/inverse hook placement.

## Validation

- 14 native tests: original source **11 failed, 3 passed**; patched source **14 passed**.
- Grayscale flips and RGB channel permutations are compared with explicit transform → UViT → inverse-transform composition. Two SGD updates compare exact outputs, input gradients, every parameter gradient and final parameters.
- Coverage includes no patching, convolutional patching and dual patch normalization.
- Real GaussianDiffusion performs two Adam updates and sampling with grayscale/RGB and patch sizes 1/2.
- Invalid inverse shapes are still rejected, while absent or single-hook paths retain their outputs.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. This repairs the paired-hook constructor for the existing shape-preserving interface; it does not infer changed convolution input channels for channel-expanding transforms. GPU execution and a full training benchmark were not run.

prs.title: Honor custom initial widths in the guided Unet
prs.body:
## Problem

The guided Unet's decoder and initial skip connection both produce `init_dim` channels, but its final residual block expects `2 * dim` channels. Setting `init_dim` to a value other than `dim` therefore fails at the last convolution during both training and sampling.

## Change

Size the final residual block and output projection using `init_dim`, matching the actual concatenated features and the corresponding layers in the other Unet variants. With the default `init_dim=dim`, parameter names, shapes and initialization order remain unchanged.

## Validation

- 18 native tests: original source **12 failed, 6 passed**; patched source **18 passed**.
- Two Adam updates with initial widths 4, 8 and 16 around a backbone width of 8, one/two resolution stages, and self-conditioning enabled/disabled. Tests check finite gradients, nonzero endpoint gradients and updated input weights.
- Native DDPM and DDIM sampling with custom widths and RGB self-conditioning.
- State-dictionary save/load restores exact outputs for each training configuration.
- Default and explicit matching widths have exactly equal initialized state dictionaries and outputs.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. No GPU execution, full training or image-quality benchmark was run.

prs.title: Evaluate learned-variance loss terms in float32 for low-precision inputs
prs.body:
## Problem

The learned-variance objective evaluates Gaussian KL and discretized Gaussian log likelihood in the input tensor dtype. In float16, a zero mean difference multiplied by an overflowing inverse variance can produce NaN; the likelihood probability floor of 1e-15 also underflows to zero. These failures reach the hybrid loss and its gradients during native half-precision training. Bfloat16 avoids the same exponent overflow but still loses precision in the small bin probabilities.

## Change

Promote float16 and bfloat16 tensor arguments to float32 inside the two loss helpers. Preserve float32/float64 and scalar inputs, the probability floor, the objective formula and the gradient path to the model parameters. The low-precision helpers now return float32 values.

## Validation

- 13 new native regression and control cases: unchanged source **8 failed, 5 passed**; patched source **13 passed**.
- Real Unet and LearnedGaussianDiffusion training for two SGD updates in float16, bfloat16 and float32, using CPU autocast for the two low-precision cases. Each loss is checked against an independent double-precision KL and scalar CDF reference; parameter gradients remain finite and the variance head receives nonzero gradients.
- Standalone half-precision zero-mean KL and likelihood-tail regressions check finite values and gradients.
- Four dtype cases compare KL values and derivatives with torch.distributions, and likelihood values and derivatives with independently calculated scalar bin probabilities, including endpoint, tail, small-variance and probability-floor cases.
- Ruff on the new tests and git diff --cached --check pass.

Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. These tests cover the stated finite inputs and native CPU training path; they do not establish bounds for arbitrary extreme float32 inputs or unrepresentable half-precision gradients. GPU execution and the full repository suite were not run.

prs.title: Accumulate FID moments without retaining feature batches
prs.body:
## Problem

FID evaluation retains every real or generated feature batch on the feature device, concatenates the full population, and only then computes its mean and covariance. Feature storage therefore grows with the requested sample count in both phases.

## Change

Accumulate batch means and centered second moments in CPU float64 using the parallel variance-combination formula. Release completed feature batches and calculate the unbiased covariance from the merged moments. Persistent statistics use O(D²) memory rather than retaining O(ND) features; per-batch working memory remains necessary.

Keep the existing loader iteration, generated sample grouping, and dataset_stats.npz field names. Existing caches still load normally. Populations with fewer than two features now raise a clear error before writing an invalid cache. The separate sample-budget correction in #395 is not duplicated.

The mean is now accumulated in float64, so exact float32 rounding is intentionally not preserved. CPU covariance work and device-to-host transfers remain, and their cost depends on batch size and feature dimension.

## Validation

- 20 new cases: original source 4 failed, 16 passed; patched source 20 passed. The failures concern retained feature batches and invalid zero/singleton populations. Numerical controls also pass on the original implementation.
- Statistics and FID values are compared with independent full-population NumPy calculations across float32/float64, singleton batches, partial final batches, high-offset populations, and cache reloads.
- Both real and generated phases check that completed feature tensors are released.
- Actual Unet/GaussianDiffusion sampling and native convolutional feature extraction/pooling are exercised for grayscale and RGB. Inception is replaced by explicitly controlled feature extractors to avoid pretrained-weight downloads; these tests do not measure image quality.
- Ruff and git diff --cached --check pass.

A local CPU statistics benchmark used 32,768 × 256 float32 features in batches of 256, with a seeded generator and three fresh processes per version. It includes feature construction, moment collection and cache writing; it excludes Inception and diffusion generation.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Peak live feature tensors | 32 MiB | 0.25 MiB |
| Median process peak RSS | 445.684 MiB | 320.430 MiB |
| Median additional peak RSS during collection | 135.664 MiB | 10.098 MiB |
| Median collection time | 0.198 s | 0.110 s |

Maximum cached-mean difference was 7.63e-8 and covariance difference 1.12e-15. These measurements establish a local CPU memory reduction; they are not GPU-memory or end-to-end speed claims. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu. GPU execution, pretrained Inception and the full repository suite were not run.

prs.title: Synchronize DDP gradients once per accumulated update
prs.body:
## Problem

Each microbatch in the four Trainer loops performs a DDP gradient reduction, even though the optimizer updates only after gradient_accumulate_every microbatches. The intermediate reductions add communication without changing the accumulated update.

## Change

For actual DistributedDataParallel models, wrap both forward and backward in Accelerator.no_sync during non-final microbatches. The final microbatch synchronizes the accumulated gradients before the existing clipping and optimizer step. Apply the same correction to the standard, 1D, guided and RePaint trainers.

Loss scaling, clipping, Adam/EMA updates and the single-process path remain unchanged. Other distributed wrapper types retain their existing path; this does not change FSDP or DeepSpeed accumulation semantics.

## Validation

The [native CPU CI comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/actions/runs/43267340545) checks out production commit d870451a94050ce0c73e444649a6e19742dcc605 and runs the same tests against it and unchanged source c8155b1dc622e3f1ef0d53dc6e5a570ca105bcec:

- Patched: **16 passed**. Unchanged source: **4 failed, 12 passed**, with zero errors or skipped tests.
- Eight cases use real two-process Gloo DDP; eight are single-process controls. Every trainer runs two actual Unet/GaussianDiffusion training steps with accumulation factors 1 and 3.
- Recorded inputs and RNG states are replayed through an independent model. Per-parameter gradients after clipping and Adam updates are compared with a reference that averages accumulated gradients once at the update boundary.
- Native DDP communication hooks count actual all-reduce calls. The small models fit in one bucket: with three microbatches, reductions change from [3, 6] cumulatively across the two updates to [1, 2]. The accumulation=1 controls already use [1, 2].
- Final parameters agree exactly across both ranks.
- Ruff on the regression module and git diff --cached --check pass.

Linux, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu, Accelerate 1.11.0. Local single-process checks also passed; the local environment disallows Gloo socket initialization, so distributed results were established in the linked CI. The validation workflow resides on a separate fork branch and is not part of this PR.

This reduces DDP communication calls for these native models. GPU/NCCL timing, multi-bucket or unused-parameter topologies, FSDP/DeepSpeed execution and the full repository suite were not tested; no end-to-end speedup is claimed.

prs.title: Honor data normalization in interpolation APIs
prs.body:
## Problem

The interpolation methods pass user images directly into q_sample and return model-space values directly. They bypass the normalization convention used by forward and sample. With automatic normalization enabled, inputs in [0, 1] therefore enter a denoising chain trained on [-1, 1], and its output is not converted back. This affects the standard, 1D, guided, RePaint and classifier-conditioned variants; the classifier-conditioned example also passes its training images directly to interpolate.

## Change

Normalize both interpolation inputs before corruption and unnormalize the returned image. Use each configurable variant's existing normalize/unnormalize functions, preserving auto_normalize=False. The classifier-conditioned variant follows its existing always-normalized training and sampling convention.

## Validation

- 18 native cases: upstream base 10 failed, 8 passed; patched branch 18 passed.
- Actual Unets in all five variants are compared with explicit conversion into and out of model space. Cases include self-conditioning, class labels, t=0 and t=2, disabled normalization, input immutability and exact RNG consumption.
- The same 18 cases also pass with the separate #381 reverse-timestep correction applied. The tests do not encode a particular loop boundary, and this patch does not duplicate that correction.
- Ruff on the regression module and git diff --cached --check pass. Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu; GPU, pretrained models and the full repository suite were not run.

This restores the input/output convention. It adds no output clipping and does not claim all intermediate/noisy results lie in [0, 1], or establish an image-quality improvement.

prs.title: Preserve best FID when resuming standard and RePaint trainers
prs.body:
## Problem

The standard and RePaint trainers reset best_fid to their initial sentinel when constructed, but their checkpoints do not save or restore that value. After resuming a run with save_best_and_latest_only enabled, the next finite FID is treated as a new best even when it is worse than the score that produced model-best.pt. A valid best checkpoint can be overwritten.

## Change

Include best_fid in best/latest-mode checkpoints and restore it when loading in that mode. Regular checkpoints do not require the field. Legacy checkpoints without the field retain the trainer's existing fallback value.

## Validation

- 10 native workflow cases: upstream base 6 failed, 4 passed; patched branch 10 passed.
- Both trainer variants perform real CPU Unet/GaussianDiffusion training with Accelerator, Adam, EMA and 100 local image files, then save, construct a new trainer, load and train again.
- Better/equal/worse score inputs check selection after resumption. Equal or worse scores leave model-best.pt byte-for-byte unchanged; an improved score replaces it at the new step. Latest checkpoints preserve the score and step, and model parameters actually update.
- Legacy-field and regular-mode controls pass.
- FID values are controlled metric inputs to isolate checkpoint decisions without downloading Inception weights; this is not an FID or image-quality benchmark. DataLoader workers are set to zero in the tests.
- Ruff on the regression module and git diff --cached --check pass. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu and Accelerate 1.11.0. GPU, distributed training and the full repository suite were not run.

prs.title: Keep one-step elucidated diffusion sampling finite
prs.body:
## Problem

The elucidated-diffusion schedule divides by `num_sample_steps - 1`. With one sampling step, its first sigma becomes NaN, and both the Euler/Heun and DPM++ samplers return non-finite images. This prevents using their existing `num_sample_steps=1` configuration.

## Change

For a single step, retain the initial sigma_max and the terminal zero, giving one transition to the denoised estimate. Preserve the existing interpolation for two or more steps. Reject zero or negative step counts before schedule generation.

## Validation

- 14 native regression cases: upstream base 11 failed, 3 passed; patched branch 14 passed.
- Real Unet runs for both sampling methods match an independent terminal-denoising calculation and perform exactly one model forward.
- Both constructor-level and per-call one-step settings are covered.
- Two-, five- and 32-step controls verify finite monotone schedules, both endpoints, and the original interpolation formula.
- Both samplers and direct schedule calls reject zero/negative counts with the same clear ValueError.
- Ruff on the regression module and git diff --cached --check pass. CPU validation used PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu; GPU runs and sample-quality benchmarks were not performed.

This restores a numerically valid single-step path; it does not claim that one-step sampling matches the quality of a longer schedule.

prs.title: Preserve supplied noise when applying diffusion offsets
prs.body:
## Problem

Offset-noise training adds the channel offset into the caller's noise tensor in place. Reusing supplied noise therefore changes subsequent losses even after resetting the random seed, and differentiable leaf noise raises an in-place autograd error. The same operation exists in the ordinary, classifier-free and RePaint implementations.

## Change

Build the augmented noise without modifying the supplied tensor and preserve its original dtype rounding. The classifier-free `q_sample` path can additionally return the noise it actually used, so its noise/velocity training targets still match the offset-corrupted sample. Its default return remains the sampled tensor.

## Validation

- 55 native regression cases: upstream base 20 failed, 35 passed; patched branch 55 passed.
- Real small Unets cover all three implementations, noise/x0/velocity objectives, offset strength zero/nonzero, caller-supplied and internally generated noise, repeated calls with the same noise, leaf-noise gradients, and direct classifier-free q_sample calls.
- Independent forward-noise and objective calculations match the losses and every model parameter gradient. Input tensors remain unchanged.
- Float16, bfloat16 and float64 controls verify preservation of the original offset-rounding behavior.
- Ruff on the new test module and git diff --cached --check pass. CPU validation used PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu; GPU execution and a full training benchmark were not run.

This groups the three occurrences of the same input-mutation defect into one correction. It preserves the established training objective and does not claim a measured sample-quality improvement.

prs.title: Preserve the embedding dtype in Karras class conditioning
prs.body:
## Problem

The three class-conditioned Karras U-Nets convert class labels to float32 immediately before the class projection. Converting a model to float64 or a low-precision dtype also converts the projection weights, so the forced float32 input causes a matrix multiplication dtype mismatch.

## Change

Convert integer/one-hot class labels to the time embedding dtype before the class projection in the 1D, 2D and 3D models.

## Validation

The new regression runs real small models and checks integer-label/one-hot equivalence, output dtype, finite outputs, and finite input/class-projection gradients.

`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_karras_class_dtype.py -q` — 9 passed (float32, float64, bfloat16 across all three models). Three float16 cases could not run in this environment: PyTorch raises `Failed to initialize cpuinfo!` during `model.to(dtype=torch.float16)`, before the changed class-conditioning code. The float16 cases remain in the regression suite for environments supporting those CPU kernels.

The original code fails non-float32 conditioning with a matrix multiplication dtype mismatch; the float32 controls pass.

prs.title: Honor the requested real-image sample count when computing FID statistics
prs.body:
## Problem

FID real-data preprocessing counts batches using the configured generation batch size. A partial final batch can add extra real images, and a loader with a different batch size can stop before the requested sample count. The resulting mean/covariance and cached statistics do not describe the requested real-image sample budget.

## Change

Track remaining real images, trim the final batch before feature extraction, and stop once the sample budget is reached. Retain support for finite datasets that end earlier. Report progress in images.

## Validation

`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_fid_sample_count.py -q` — 6 passed on CPU with PyTorch 2.15.0.

The test uses a deterministic feature extractor to avoid pretrained-weight downloads and compares computed/cached mean and covariance with direct NumPy statistics. It covers oversized, smaller, irregular and exact batches, plus exhaustion of a short finite dataset. Against the original code, the four mismatched-batch cases fail and both controls pass.

prs.title: Fix guided DDIM sampling history to include each updated state
prs.body:
## Problem

`GaussianDiffusion.ddim_sample(return_all_timesteps=True)` in guided diffusion records the image before each update. Its history repeats the initial noise and omits the final denoised sample, so the last history frame disagrees with an otherwise identical sampling run returning only its final output.

## Change

Append each image after its DDIM update, including the terminal `x_start` update. Keep the initial noise as the first frame and preserve the existing history length.

## Validation

`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_guided_ddim_history.py -q` — 18 passed on CPU with PyTorch 2.15.0.

The regression covers all three prediction objectives, self-conditioning on/off, one/multiple sampling steps, and DDPM as a control. It checks seeded final-sample equality and the initial-noise frame using actual small U-Net sampling runs. Against the original code, 12 cases fail and the six DDPM controls pass.

prs.title: Keep RePaint resampling aligned with the current noise level
prs.body:
The RePaint resampling loop replaces the current timestep with resample_jump, adds noise only once and repeatedly denoises at that fixed timestep. The sample and schedule become misaligned; a jump larger than the schedule also raises IndexError.

Starting from the current reverse-step output, apply forward noise through the requested jump and denoise back through those same timesteps. Bound the jump by the schedule and carry self-conditioning through repeated reverse steps. This follows the traversal in the [official RePaint implementation](https://github.com/andreas128/RePaint#code-overview).

On main at c8155b1dc622e3f1ef0d53dc6e5a570ca105bcec, 4 regression cases fail and 2 controls pass; all 6 pass with this change. Coverage checks denoising schedules, closed-form forward-jump attenuation, boundaries, self-conditioning and disabled resampling with the actual sampler and U-Net on CPU.

prs.title: Respect the normalization setting for RePaint ground truth
prs.body:
RePaint always maps the ground-truth image from [0, 1] to [-1, 1], including when auto_normalize=False. Pre-normalized input is transformed again, so known pixels in the final sample no longer match the supplied image.

Use the configured self.normalize function, matching the training and output normalization settings.

prs.title: Preserve custom attention scales in the SDPA backend
prs.body:
## Problem
`Attend(flash=True, scale=s)` rescales queries by `s / d`, after which SDPA applies its own `1 / sqrt(d)`. The effective logit scale is therefore `s / d**1.5` instead of `s`.

For head width 4 and scale 1, a query [1, 0, 0, 0], keys [1, 0, 0, 0] / [0, 0, 0, 0] and values 1 / 0 produce approximately 0.531209 with SDPA versus the expected 0.731059 with eager attention.

This concerns explicitly supplied custom scales. Current built-in model call sites leave scale=None; no default-model quality improvement is claimed.

## Change
Use `q.shape[-1] ** -0.5` as the default SDPA scale when computing the query multiplier. #314 fixed the reference to `self.scale`; this corrects the remaining ratio.

## Validation
Base: c8155b1dc622e3f1ef0d53dc6e5a570ca105bcec.
Source: 4033b5eee00637a8c846d9c78c4d44bc2b041195.

prs.title: Fix interpolation reverse-timestep alignment
prs.body:
GaussianDiffusion.interpolate corrupts both inputs at timestep t but starts denoising at t−1. The first posterior uses the wrong noise level; t=0 returns the still-noisy mixture without evaluating the model.

Include t in the descending loop and progress count. This matches the existing q_sample/p_sample convention and completes the terminal transition at t=0. For t>0 it adds one model evaluation and one posterior noise draw, so results from an old random seed intentionally change.

Validation on Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu with native package imports:

- The same newly added 94-case suite gives 57 failures and 37 controls on unchanged upstream c8155b1, then 94 passes with no skips after the one-line production fix. These are the entire tracked pytest scope; the pinned upstream tree has no earlier tests.
- Posterior-chain calculations cover all three schedules, float32/float64 computation, t=0/intermediate/default endpoints, batches and interpolation weights, self-conditioning, input ownership and exact RNG consumption. Real randomly initialized Unets cover interpolation for all three objectives and self-conditioning. Separate native pred_noise training/backward and ordinary sampling controls pass.
- Wheels, compilation, new-test Ruff lint/format and git diff --check pass. Ruff 0.17.0 with F,I,UP,B,C4,PIE,FA,RUF reports 276 identical inherited diagnostics on base/final, with no new signatures. No lint/type/docs workflow is configured.

The production patches from account PRs #373, #374, #375, #376, #377 and #380 do not change this loop. Indexed all-state interpolation/off-by-one PR searches found no matching fix; indexing may be incomplete.

Scope caveat: WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion's existing p_mean_variance signature is incompatible with inherited p_sample. On unchanged base, ordinary sample/p_sample and every positive interpolation timestep already raise an x_self_cond TypeError. Its t=0 path now reaches the same error rather than returning an undenoised mixture; this patch does not repair that variant.

prs.title: Honor the selected objective in learned-variance diffusion
prs.body:
`LearnedGaussianDiffusion` inherits the default `objective='pred_v'` and accepts `pred_x0`, but its simple loss and posterior reconstruction always interpret the mean head as predicted noise. A model that exactly predicts the configured data or velocity target therefore gets a nonzero simple loss and reconstructs the wrong clean image.

Use the selected objective consistently for the simple-loss target, posterior mean, and DDIM predictions. Preserve the learned log-variance interpolation and detached mean in the variational-bound term. Clipping now leaves the raw data-prediction head available to the simple loss. The prediction conversion also honors the existing noise-rederivation argument after clipping.

Compatibility: explicitly use `objective='pred_noise'` when sampling or resuming/continuing training from checkpoints produced by the previous noise-only loss, so their mean head retains its noise-prediction meaning. The class docstring records the sampling note. This does not automatically detect a checkpoint's objective, and resumed full training was not evaluated.

Validation on Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.5.1 CPU:

- All 95 new regressions pass. They cover float32/float64 analytic targets, losses, posterior values and derivatives, Gaussian KL and detached-mean gradients, plus actual small random-initialized `Unet` backward passes and DDPM/DDIM sampling.
- On the unchanged base, 44 objective assertions fail independently of `model_predictions`. Another 27 prediction/sampling cases stop at the missing imports already reported by Anai-Guo in [#372](https://github.com/lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/pull/372). A separate control with only that PR's two learned-module import additions still has the same 44 objective failures (59 failures and 36 passes overall). This patch adds neither import; the objective-aware conversion uses a direct clamp.
- Twelve legacy `pred_noise` loss/posterior controls preserve all 84 recorded arrays exactly, including both head gradients and the timestep-zero decoder term.
- PEP 517 wheel builds, the new test's Ruff and format checks, compilation, and whitespace checks pass. Supplemental whole-repository Ruff remains red with 270 diagnostics versus 272 on the base, with no introduced diagnostics. The repository has no existing tracked test suite or PR check workflow.

Tests use native CPU execution without model downloads or tracker initialization. GPU execution, pretrained checkpoints, complete training runs, and model quality or performance evaluations were not run.

prs.title: fix: KarrasUnet3D attention crashes when attention width differs from dim
prs.body:
`KarrasUnet3D` crashes in attention for model sizes where the attention width differs from the block width:

```python
import torch
from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.karras_unet_3d import KarrasUnet3D

unet = KarrasUnet3D(frames = 4, image_size = 16, dim = 16, dim_max = 32, num_downsamples = 2, channels = 3)
unet(torch.randn(2, 3, 4, 16, 16), time = torch.rand(2))
# RuntimeError: shape '[2, 32, 2, 8, 8]' is invalid for input of size 32768
```

The attention output has `heads * dim_head` channels, and `heads = max(ceil(dim_out / attn_dim_head), 2)`, so this only equals the input dim when `dim_out` is a multiple of `attn_dim_head` and at least `2 * attn_dim_head`. `Attention.forward` reshaped the output back to the input shape before `to_out`, which fails in every other case (the same happens with `factorize_space_time_attn = True`).

This reshapes to `(b, -1, t, h, w)` instead, so `to_out` maps the hidden dim back to `dim`, the same way the 2D `KarrasUnet` does with its `rearrange`. When the two dims are equal the result is identical to before.

Checked with the snippet above (with and without factorized attention) and with `dim = 64, attn_res = (16, 8, 4)`; all now return the input shape.

prs.title: fix: WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion.sample() raises TypeError
prs.body:
`WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion.sample()` currently fails right away:

```python
import torch
from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import Unet
from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.weighted_objective_gaussian_diffusion import WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion

model = Unet(dim = 8, dim_mults = (1, 2), out_dim = 8)
diffusion = WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion(model, image_size = 32, timesteps = 10)
diffusion.sample(batch_size = 2)
# TypeError: WeightedObjectiveGaussianDiffusion.p_mean_variance() got an unexpected keyword argument 'x_self_cond'
```

`GaussianDiffusion.p_sample` calls `p_mean_variance(x = ..., t = ..., x_self_cond = ..., clip_denoised = True)` and unpacks four values (mean, variance, log variance, x_start). The override took no `x_self_cond` and returned three values.

This lets the override accept the extra keyword (as `LearnedGaussianDiffusion.p_mean_variance` already does) and return the weighted x_start as the fourth value. Training is unchanged. With the fix, the snippet above returns a `(2, 3, 32, 32)` tensor in [0, 1].

prs.title: fix: keep CFG rescaling finite for zero-variance predictions
prs.body:
## Problem

CFG standard-deviation rescaling divides by zero for constant guided predictions; the default sample standard deviation is also undefined for one value per sample. Finite model outputs can become NaN.

## Fix

Use population standard deviations, promote half/bfloat16 statistics to float32, and leave a zero-variance sample unrescaled. Regular nondegenerate ratios retain the original formula within floating-point tolerance. Invalid network outputs are not globally sanitized. This does not include or duplicate the unit-scale return-contract change in #374.

## Validation

```shell
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_cfg_finite_rescale.py -q
```

**17 passed, no skips** on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12.14 and official PyTorch 2.6.0+cpu. The independent fork workflow checks out this PR head `523f151acf5b9f36c24fe01411bde6e01c4a4552` directly: [successful validation job](https://github.com/Afloat16/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/actions/runs/36678619311/job/109768971091). The validation workflow is on a separate branch and is not part of this PR.

All cases now pass, including the three float16 cases previously blocked by unavailable /proc/cpuinfo in the local environment. No tests were skipped or weakened. The cases cover float16/float32/float64/bfloat16, constant and single-element outputs, per-sample fallback, finite gradients, preservation of invalid model outputs, and a real zero-output Unet with DDIM sampling. `git diff --check` passes.

For comparison, clean main c8155b1 produced 13 failures and 4 passes in the restricted local environment. The previous local draft blocker is resolved by the successful hosted run.

No GPU run, full training, or image-quality benchmark has been performed. This is not a claim to fix arbitrary overflow.

prs.title: fix: align immiscible training targets with assigned noise
prs.body:
## Problem

With `immiscible=True`, `q_sample` permutes the noise batch using linear assignment, but `p_losses` builds pred_noise/pred_v targets from the original noise. A predictor returning the exact assigned target can therefore receive nonzero loss and incorrect gradients.

## Change

Allow `q_sample` to optionally return the actual noise alongside the sample, and use that noise for the main 2D GaussianDiffusion training target. The default tensor return is preserved; assignment runs once. When immiscible mode is disabled, p_losses still calls the old q_sample signature, so existing overrides continue working in that mode.

Custom q_sample overrides used with immiscible=True must support the new `return_noise` keyword and pair return. No in-repository override of this main class method was found. Subclasses with their own loss implementations are outside this fix.

## Validation

```shell
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_immiscible_targets.py -q
```

18 passed using normal package imports on Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.6.0+cpu. The same tests on clean main c8155b1 give 8 failures and 10 passes. Tests cover all objectives, minimum-SNR weighting, identity/nonidentity assignments, immiscible disabled, caller input nonmutation, one assignment per call, analytic loss/gradient references, legacy q_sample overrides when disabled, and two real small Unet loss/backward checks. `git diff --check` passes.

No full GPU training or image-quality benchmark was run. This is separate from the existing CFG return-contract PR #374.

prs.title: fix: return conditional and unconditional predictions at unit CFG scale
prs.body:
## Problem

In `classifier_free_guidance.py`, `Unet.forward_with_cond_scale` returns only a tensor when `cond_scale == 1`, but `GaussianDiffusion.model_predictions` always unpacks `(model_output, model_output_null)`. Batches of size 1 or greater than 2 raise unpacking errors. A batch of size 2 instead unpacks its samples, losing the batch dimension and mixing predictions between samples through broadcasting.

## Change

Return `(logits, null_logits)` at unit scale, consistently with other scales. Compute the actual unconditional forward pass before that return because CFG++ uses it for its noise prediction; substituting conditional logits would change CFG++ semantics. This adds the unconditional pass at unit scale, including when CFG++ is disabled. Other guidance scales and rescaling behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

```shell
python -m pytest tests/test_cfg_unit_scale.py -q
```

61 passed using real, randomly initialized CPU Unets and normal package imports (Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0+cpu, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu). On unchanged main c8155b1, the same file has 37 failures and 24 passes.

Coverage includes batch sizes 1/2/3/4, all three objectives, CFG++ on/off, batch permutation consistency, a non-unit-scale control, DDIM/DDPM sampling, and finite gradients. The expected conditional and unconditional predictions are computed with separate real forward calls. `git diff --check` passes. No GPU training or image-quality benchmark was run.

Searched existing cond_scale issues and PRs before opening; no matching return-contract fix found.

Two submodules reference names that are never imported, so exercising them raises `NameError`. Both fixes mirror how the main `denoising_diffusion_pytorch.py` module already handles the same names.

### 1. `guided_diffusion.py` — `Trainer.save()` crashes on `__version__`

`save()` builds the checkpoint dict with `'version': __version__` (line 888), but the import is commented out:

```python
# from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.version import __version__
```

So the very first checkpoint save raises `NameError: name '__version__' is not defined`. The main module keeps this import active (`denoising_diffusion_pytorch.py`) and uses `'version': __version__` in its own `save()` the same way. Fix: uncomment the import.

### 2. `learned_gaussian_diffusion.py` — `model_predictions()` crashes on `partial` / `identity`

Line 90:

```python
maybe_clip = partial(torch.clamp, min = -1., max = 1.) if clip_x_start else identity
```

Neither `partial` nor `identity` is imported in this file, so any call to `LearnedGaussianDiffusion.model_predictions()` (i.e. any sampling) raises `NameError`. The main module imports `from functools import partial` and defines `def identity(t, *args, **kwargs)`. Fix: add `from functools import partial` and pull `identity` from the main module via the existing import line.

### Verification

Extracted each function with `ast` and replayed it with stubbed state:

```
save              before -> NameError: name '__version__' is not defined ; after -> OK (checkpoint written)
model_predictions before -> NameError: name 'partial' is not defined     ; after -> passes line 90
```

Both changes are import-only (+2 / -1 across two files); no behavior change beyond removing the crash.

prs.title: fix: SinusoidalPosEmb crashes under .half() with standard long timesteps
prs.body:
## What

`SinusoidalPosEmb.forward` returns whatever dtype `x[:, None] * emb[None, :]` happens to promote to. `emb` is always float32 (`torch.arange` with no `dtype=`, promoted further by the `-emb` float multiply), so the result stays float32 regardless of `x`'s dtype — including when `x` is the standard `long` timestep tensor (see `p_sample_loop`'s `.long()`).

Once `time_mlp = nn.Sequential(SinusoidalPosEmb(dim), nn.Linear(...), ...)` is `.half()`'d (a normal inference-speedup path), `SinusoidalPosEmb` has no parameters for `.half()` to touch, so it keeps emitting float32 — and the next `Linear`'s now-float16 weights crash on it:

```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype, but got Float and Half
```

This reproduces with realistic `long` timesteps, not just an unusual float16-timestep edge case — confirmed end-to-end on the actual `Unet`/`GaussianDiffusion` classes:

```python
model = Unet(dim=16, dim_mults=(1,2)).half()
t = torch.randint(0, 10, (2,)).long()
model(torch.randn(2, 3, 32, 32).half(), t)  # RuntimeError on main
```

## Fix

A non-persistent dummy buffer (`_dtype_ref`, an empty tensor) purely to track the module's own working dtype through `Module.to()`/`.half()`, independent of `x`'s dtype. `x` itself can't be used for this (`.type_as(x)` would truncate the sin/cos output to integers whenever `x` is `long` — I tried this first, verified it breaks the common case, then switched to the buffer). `forward` now returns `emb.to(self._dtype_ref.dtype)`.

Applied the same fix to all 5 files defining this exact class — confirmed via `grep` these are the only occurrences: `classifier_free_guidance.py`, `denoising_diffusion_pytorch.py`, `denoising_diffusion_pytorch_1d.py`, `guided_diffusion.py`, `repaint.py`.

The sibling `RandomOrLearnedSinusoidalPosEmb` (same files) and `MPFourierEmbedding` (`karras_unet*.py`) classes use a real `nn.Parameter` for their frequency weights, so `.half()` already moves them correctly — left untouched, confirmed via the same direct-execution testing.

## Testing

No test suite exists in this repo, so verified directly by execution:
- Baseline float32 output is bit-identical to the pre-fix behavior (`long` timesteps, float32 model) — confirmed via `torch.equal`.
- The crash scenario (`.half()`'d `time_mlp`/`Unet`, `long` timesteps) now runs and produces correctly float16-typed, non-zero output.
- Explicit `.to(dtype=torch.float64)` on the module correctly propagates too.
- Confirmed red (exact `RuntimeError`) on unpatched code, green with the fix, on both the isolated `SinusoidalPosEmb` class and the full `Unet.forward()` path.
- Full `Unet` + `GaussianDiffusion` float32 forward/backward pass still works (no regression to the standard training path).

Found via a static architectural-bug scanner (a personal tool) flagging the general "sin/cos forward with no cast-back to the caller's dtype" shape — same bug class as the already-merged `rotary-embedding-torch#50`.

prs.title: Fix min-SNR loss weight clamp direction in continuous time diffusion
prs.body:
## Summary

The min-SNR-gamma strategy ([Hang et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09556)) computes loss weights as `min(SNR(t), gamma) / SNR(t)` to down-weight high-SNR (low-noise) timesteps during training.

In `continuous_time_gaussian_diffusion.py`, the clamp uses `min` instead of `max`:

```python
# Before (wrong) — computes max(SNR, gamma) / SNR
loss_weight = snr.clamp(min = self.min_snr_gamma) / snr

# After (correct) — computes min(SNR, gamma) / SNR
loss_weight = snr.clamp(max = self.min_snr_gamma) / snr
```

`torch.clamp(min=gamma)` gives `max(SNR, gamma)`, which inverts the intended behavior — it up-weights high-SNR timesteps rather than down-weighting them. The fix changes this to `clamp(max=gamma)` which gives `min(SNR, gamma)`, matching the paper and all other diffusion modules in this repo (e.g., `denoising_diffusion_pytorch.py`, `simple_diffusion.py`, `classifier_free_guidance.py`, etc. all correctly use `clamp_(max=...)`).

prs.title: Fix RePaint: use ground-truth in the last in-painting step
prs.body:
Dear @lucidrains,

I have found an imperfection of the RePaint method. In the last in-painting step (when t=1 and we denoise the image to get the restored x_{t=0}) the ground-truth image is not used in the area were the mask is positive. This leads to more blurry images as @nilsleh mentioned in another issue.

By using the ground-truth image (provided as input alongside the mask) in the last step, we make sure that we use the real image where we are not meant to reconstruct any missing part, and we only perform the RePaint algorithm in the missing section marked with the mask.

Let me know if any questions 👍

prs.title: Robust batched FID calculation
prs.body:
Implements #224 and fixes #226.

- Includes a separate `fid_evaluation.py` that houses the `FIDEvaluation` class which can be used out-of-the-box if needed to evaluate any sampler with a `sample` method.
- `FIDEvaluation` provides the means for robust FID evaluation with an arbitrary number of samples and batch size. This class automatically caches dataset stats into a file called `dataset_stats.npz` under `self.results_dir` of the `Trainer` class for future use. It attempts to read the stats from this file if it exists.
- Integrated the new `FIDEvaluation` class into the `Trainer` class previously available.
- Provided the option for the `Trainer` class to only save the `best` (as determined by FID) and `latest` models as opposed to saving the model at every milestone (defaults to `False` to preserve backward compatibility).
- Since `inception_block_idx` is exposed as a keyword argument, hot-fixed the current FID computation method to accommodate dimensions other than 2048.
- Replaced `torch.no_grad()` decorators and context managers with `torch.inference_mode()` according to [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69543907/pytorch-torch-no-grad-vs-torch-inference-mode) and [this](https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/pytorch-torch-no-grad-vs-torch-inference-mode/134099).

**Further suggestions:**
- Using the solvers provided by the `diffusers` library to outsource the sampling procedure. There are several solvers that are able to sample high quality with as few as 20 inference steps. This not only tremendously helps with cutting down the FID calculation time but also ensures that current state-of-the-art sampling techniques integrated into `diffusers` can be used with modifying a few lines of code at a time.
- Moving the utility functions and operations into their respective modules (e.g. `utils.py` and `ops.py`) to isolate only the diffusion code within each separate file for improved readability.

prs.title: eta=0
prs.body:
Shouldn't eta be 0 for DDIM sampling? In the DDIM paper in section 5.1 they mention the eta=0 is DDIM, and eta=1 approximates the normal DDPM. They also use [eta=0](https://github.com/openai/improved-diffusion/blob/e94489283bb876ac1477d5dd7709bbbd2d9902ce/improved_diffusion/gaussian_diffusion.py#L487) in the openai implementation of DDIM.

Maybe I'm missing something, but I figured I would make the PR just in case.

prs.title: Added gradient clipping.
prs.body: This PR fixes #61 and #101. I looked at the maximum of the model gradients during learning and often some gradients can become very big: I added gradient clipping, which is also used by many other repositories of stable diffusion models. The training loss is more stable, I didn't get the NaN problem with amp=True anymore (cyan is before PR, magenta is after): I think this may also fix the loss divergence issues I encountered, but I haven't tested enough so far. It may be due to the high gradients shooting the model's weights somewhere where gradients are higher which leads to divergence. I saw someone else having [the same issue here](https://github.com/lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch/issues/4#issuecomment-860757983).

prs.title: Trainer.load can use GPU's other than cuda:0
prs.body:
Hi! When I tried to load a checkpoint while using GPU 1 (because I'm sharing a computer with my other labmates), it decided to take up VRAM on both GPU 0 and GPU 1. This is because by default torch.load uses VRAM on cuda:0. I've added a fix; now this code will only use VRAM on the device set by the user.

```
#Code from https://github.com/lucidrains/denoising-diffusion-pytorch

import torch
from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import Unet, GaussianDiffusion, Trainer

dataset_path='/my/image/folder'


device=torch.device('cuda:1')
torch.cuda.set_device(device)

model = Unet(
    dim = 64,
    dim_mults = (1, 2, 4, 8)
).to(device)

diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(
    model,
    image_size = 128,
    timesteps = 1000,           # number of steps
    sampling_timesteps = 250,   # number of sampling timesteps (using ddim for faster inference [see citation for ddim paper])
    loss_type = 'l1'            # L1 or L2
).to(device)

trainer = Trainer(
    diffusion,
    dataset_path,
    train_batch_size = 32
    train_lr = 8e-5,
    train_num_steps = 700000,         # total training steps
    gradient_accumulate_every = 2,    # gradient accumulation steps
    ema_decay = 0.995,                # exponential moving average decay
    amp = False,                        # turn on mixed precision
    results_folder = './results',
)

trainer.load(11)

trainer.train()
```

prs.title: fix pred_noise after clipping denoised
prs.body:
I've been comparing the recent changes to the DDIM sampling code against Glide's implementation to verify that it's doing the same thing given the same starting points and model (I used a simple random 1D model) and found that there might be a mistake in how clipping the denoised x_0 is being processed here.

In Glide's implementation, the predicted noise is being [recomputed](https://github.com/openai/glide-text2im/blob/main/glide_text2im/gaussian_diffusion.py#L482) after [clipping the predicted x_0](https://github.com/openai/glide-text2im/blob/main/glide_text2im/gaussian_diffusion.py#L253). In our implementation, we predict both x_0 and noise in .model_predictions() but then clip only x_start, which leaves pred_noise as it was and inconsistent with the x_start being used later to compute x_t-1. I'm not sure but I think it makes sense to update the predicted noise after clipping as well, and it's also what Glide does.

+"""Batch and CFG++ regressions using a real, randomly initialized CPU Unet."""
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.classifier_free_guidance import GaussianDiffusion, Unet, project
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def model():
+    threads = torch.get_num_threads()
+    torch.set_num_threads(1)
+    torch.manual_seed(178)
+    yield Unet(dim=8, num_classes=3, dim_mults=(1, 2), channels=1).eval()
+    torch.set_num_threads(threads)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('batch', [1, 2, 3, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('objective', ['pred_noise', 'pred_x0', 'pred_v'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('cfg_plus_plus', [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('scale', [1., 3.])
+def test_prediction_batch_and_unconditional_branch(model, batch, objective, cfg_plus_plus, scale):
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(model, image_size=8, timesteps=8,
+                                  objective=objective, use_cfg_plus_plus=cfg_plus_plus)
+    x = torch.randn(batch, 1, 8, 8)
+    t = torch.ones(batch, dtype=torch.long)
+    classes = torch.arange(batch) % 3
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        conditional = model(x, t, classes, cond_drop_prob=0.)
+        unconditional = model(x, t, classes, cond_drop_prob=1.)
+        assert not torch.allclose(conditional, unconditional)
+        _, orthogonal = project(conditional - unconditional, conditional)
+        guided = conditional if scale == 1. else conditional + orthogonal * (scale - 1.)
+        noise_output = unconditional if cfg_plus_plus else guided
+
+        def to_start(output):
+            if objective == 'pred_noise':
+                return diffusion.predict_start_from_noise(x, t, output)
+            if objective == 'pred_v':
+                return diffusion.predict_start_from_v(x, t, output)
+            return output
+
+        expected_start = to_start(guided)
+        expected_noise = noise_output if objective == 'pred_noise' else diffusion.predict_noise_from_start(x, t, to_start(noise_output))
+        prediction = diffusion.model_predictions(x, t, classes, cond_scale=scale, rescaled_phi=0.)
+        assert prediction.pred_noise.shape == x.shape
+        assert prediction.pred_x_start.shape == x.shape
+        torch.testing.assert_close(prediction.pred_noise, expected_noise)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(prediction.pred_x_start, expected_start)
+        permutation = torch.arange(batch - 1, -1, -1)
+        permuted = diffusion.model_predictions(x[permutation], t[permutation], classes[permutation], cond_scale=scale, rescaled_phi=0.)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(permuted.pred_noise, prediction.pred_noise[permutation])
+        torch.testing.assert_close(permuted.pred_x_start, prediction.pred_x_start[permutation])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('sampling_steps', [2, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('cfg_plus_plus', [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('objective', ['pred_noise', 'pred_x0', 'pred_v'])
+def test_unit_scale_ddim_and_ddpm(model, sampling_steps, cfg_plus_plus, objective):
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(model, image_size=8, timesteps=4, sampling_timesteps=sampling_steps,
+                                  objective=objective, use_cfg_plus_plus=cfg_plus_plus)
+    result = diffusion.sample(classes=torch.tensor([0, 1, 2]), cond_scale=1., rescaled_phi=0.)
+    assert result.shape == (3, 1, 8, 8)
+    assert torch.isfinite(result).all()
+
+
+def test_unit_scale_helper_returns_both_predictions_with_finite_gradients(model):
+    x = torch.randn(3, 1, 8, 8, requires_grad=True)
+    t = torch.ones(3, dtype=torch.long)
+    classes = torch.arange(3)
+    outputs = model.forward_with_cond_scale(x, t, classes, cond_scale=1.)
+    assert isinstance(outputs, tuple) and len(outputs) == 2
+    conditional, unconditional = outputs
+    torch.testing.assert_close(conditional, model(x, t, classes, cond_drop_prob=0.))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(unconditional, model(x, t, classes, cond_drop_prob=1.))
+    (conditional.square().mean() + unconditional.square().mean()).backward()
+    assert torch.isfinite(x.grad).all()
+    assert all(torch.isfinite(p.grad).all() for p in model.parameters() if p.grad is not None)

+import pytest
+import torch
+from accelerate import Accelerator
+from accelerate.state import PartialState
+from ema_pytorch import EMA
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import Trainer, Trainer1D
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.guided_diffusion import Trainer as GuidedTrainer
+
+
+def make_trainer(trainer_type, rank, folder, monkeypatch):
+    accelerator = Accelerator(cpu=True)
+    state = PartialState()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(state, "process_index", rank)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(state, "local_process_index", rank % 2)
+    trainer = trainer_type.__new__(trainer_type)
+    trainer.accelerator = accelerator
+    trainer.model = torch.nn.Linear(2, 2)
+    trainer.opt = torch.optim.Adam(trainer.model.parameters())
+    trainer.model(torch.ones(1, 2)).sum().backward()
+    trainer.opt.step()
+    trainer.step = 13
+    trainer.results_folder = folder
+    if accelerator.is_main_process:
+        trainer.ema = EMA(trainer.model)
+    return trainer
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("trainer_type", [Trainer, Trainer1D, GuidedTrainer])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rank", [1, 2])
+def test_nonowner_does_not_write_checkpoint(trainer_type, rank, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    trainer = make_trainer(trainer_type, rank, tmp_path, monkeypatch)
+    path = tmp_path / "model-3.pt"
+    path.write_bytes(b"existing checkpoint")
+    trainer.save(3)
+    assert path.read_bytes() == b"existing checkpoint"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("trainer_type", [Trainer, Trainer1D])
+def test_owner_saves_model_optimizer_and_ema(trainer_type, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    trainer = make_trainer(trainer_type, 0, tmp_path, monkeypatch)
+    trainer.save(3)
+    checkpoint = torch.load(tmp_path / "model-3.pt", weights_only=True)
+    assert checkpoint["step"] == trainer.step
+    assert checkpoint["opt"]["state"]
+    for key, value in trainer.model.state_dict().items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(checkpoint["model"][key], value)
+    for key, value in trainer.ema.state_dict().items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(checkpoint["ema"][key], value)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rank", [0, 1, 2])
+def test_guided_checkpoint_restores_training_state_on_every_rank(rank, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    source = make_trainer(Trainer, 0, tmp_path, monkeypatch)
+    source.save(3)
+    checkpoint = torch.load(tmp_path / "model-3.pt", weights_only=True)
+    restored = make_trainer(GuidedTrainer, rank, tmp_path, monkeypatch)
+    restored.step = 0
+    restored.load(3)
+    assert restored.step == checkpoint["step"]
+    for key, value in restored.model.state_dict().items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(value, checkpoint["model"][key])
+    for actual, expected in zip(restored.opt.state_dict()["state"].values(), checkpoint["opt"]["state"].values()):
+        for key in actual:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual[key], expected[key])
+    if rank == 0:
+        for key, value in restored.ema.state_dict().items():
+            torch.testing.assert_close(value, checkpoint["ema"][key])

+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import Unet
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.guided_diffusion import GaussianDiffusion
+
+
+class ZeroPrediction(nn.Module):
+    channels = out_dim = 1
+    self_condition = False
+    random_or_learned_sinusoidal_cond = False
+
+    def forward(self, image, time, self_cond=None):
+        return torch.zeros_like(image)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("objective", ["pred_noise", "pred_x0", "pred_v"])
+def test_one_step_guidance_matches_conditional_score(objective):
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(
+        ZeroPrediction(), image_size=4, timesteps=8, sampling_timesteps=1,
+        objective=objective, auto_normalize=False,
+    )
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    initial = torch.randn(2, 1, 4, 4)
+    alpha = diffusion.alphas_cumprod[-1]
+    if objective == "pred_noise":
+        denoised = (initial / alpha.sqrt()).clamp(-1, 1)
+    elif objective == "pred_x0":
+        denoised = torch.zeros_like(initial)
+    else:
+        denoised = (alpha.sqrt() * initial).clamp(-1, 1)
+
+    gradient = torch.full_like(initial, 0.01)
+    expected = denoised + (1 - alpha) / alpha.sqrt() * gradient
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    result = diffusion.sample(batch_size=2, cond_fn=lambda image, time: gradient)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result, expected, atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-4)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("objective", ["pred_noise", "pred_x0", "pred_v"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sampling_steps", [1, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("eta", [0.0, 0.5])
+def test_native_unet_ddim_uses_classifier_gradients(objective, sampling_steps, eta):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = Unet(
+        dim=8, dim_mults=(1,), channels=1, attn_heads=1, attn_dim_head=4,
+        self_condition=True,
+    )
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(
+        model, image_size=4, timesteps=8, sampling_timesteps=sampling_steps,
+        objective=objective, ddim_sampling_eta=eta,
+    ).eval()
+    calls = []
+
+    def classifier_gradient(image, time, *, target, strength):
+        calls.append(time.clone())
+        with torch.enable_grad():
+            image = image.detach().requires_grad_(True)
+            log_probability = -strength * (image - target).square().sum() / 2
+            return torch.autograd.grad(log_probability, image)[0]
+
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    unconditioned = diffusion.sample(batch_size=2)
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    conditioned = diffusion.sample(
+        batch_size=2, cond_fn=classifier_gradient,
+        guidance_kwargs={"target": 0.3, "strength": 0.01},
+    )
+
+    expected_times = [7] if sampling_steps == 1 else [7, 5, 3, 1]
+    assert [time[0].item() for time in calls] == expected_times
+    assert all(time.shape == (2,) and torch.equal(time, time[:1].expand(2)) for time in calls)
+    assert conditioned.shape == (2, 1, 4, 4)
+    assert torch.isfinite(conditioned).all()
+    assert not torch.allclose(conditioned, unconditioned)
+    assert not conditioned.requires_grad
+    assert all(parameter.grad is None for parameter in model.parameters())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("objective", ["pred_noise", "pred_x0", "pred_v"])
+def test_zero_guidance_preserves_single_step_prediction(objective):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = Unet(dim=8, dim_mults=(1,), channels=1, attn_heads=1, attn_dim_head=4)
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(
+        model, image_size=4, timesteps=8, sampling_timesteps=1, objective=objective,
+    ).eval()
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    expected = diffusion.sample(batch_size=2)
+    torch.manual_seed(12)
+    actual = diffusion.sample(batch_size=2, cond_fn=lambda image, time: torch.zeros_like(image))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-4)

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import Unet
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.elucidated_diffusion import ElucidatedDiffusion
+
+
+def make_diffusion():
+    net = Unet(
+        dim=8,
+        dim_mults=(1,),
+        channels=1,
+        random_fourier_features=True,
+        attn_heads=1,
+        attn_dim_head=4,
+    )
+    return ElucidatedDiffusion(net, image_size=4, channels=1, S_churn=0).eval()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("steps", [1, 2, 8])
+def test_sampling_schedule_reaches_zero(steps):
+    diffusion = make_diffusion()
+    schedule = diffusion.sample_schedule(steps)
+    fractions = torch.linspace(0, 1, steps, dtype=torch.float64)
+    expected = (
+        diffusion.sigma_max ** (1 / diffusion.rho)
+        + fractions * (
+            diffusion.sigma_min ** (1 / diffusion.rho)
+            - diffusion.sigma_max ** (1 / diffusion.rho)
+        )
+    ) ** diffusion.rho
+    expected = torch.cat((expected, torch.zeros(1))).float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(schedule, expected)
+    assert (schedule[:-1] > schedule[1:]).all()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["sample", "sample_using_dpmpp"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("steps", [1, 4])
+def test_native_sampling_with_one_or_multiple_steps(method, steps):
+    diffusion = make_diffusion()

+import importlib
+import json
+import os
+import socket
+from datetime import timedelta
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as distributed
+import torch.multiprocessing as multiprocessing
+from PIL import Image
+from torch import nn
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import fid_evaluation
+
+
+class DeterministicInception(nn.Module):
+    """Exercise real FID statistics without downloading pretrained weights."""
+
+    BLOCK_INDEX_BY_DIM = {2048: 0}
+
+    def __init__(self, blocks):
+        super().__init__()
+
+    def forward(self, images):
+        mean = images.mean(dim=(1, 2, 3))
+        square_mean = images.square().mean(dim=(1, 2, 3))
+        return [torch.stack((mean, square_mean), dim=1)[:, :, None, None]]
+
+
+class CountedIterator:
+    def __init__(self, iterator):
+        self.iterator = iterator
+        self.next_calls = 0
+
+    def __iter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    def __next__(self):
+        value = next(self.iterator)
+        self.next_calls += 1
+        return value
+
+
+def prepare_module(variant):
+    module = importlib.import_module(f"denoising_diffusion_pytorch.{variant}")
+    original_cycle = module.cycle
+    # Count real iterator advancement; keep DataLoaderShard and its synchronization.
+    module.cycle = lambda loader: CountedIterator(original_cycle(loader))
+    module.cpu_count = lambda: 0
+    fid_evaluation.InceptionV3 = DeterministicInception
+    return module
+
+
+def make_trainer(module, folder, results_folder, calculate_fid):
+    torch.manual_seed(83)
+    model = module.Unet(
+        dim=8,
+        dim_mults=(1,),
+        channels=1,
+        attn_dim_head=4,
+        attn_heads=1,
+    )
+    diffusion = module.GaussianDiffusion(
+        model,
+        image_size=8,
+        timesteps=2,
+        sampling_timesteps=1,
+        beta_schedule="cosine",
+        objective="pred_noise",
+    )
+    return module.Trainer(
+        diffusion,
+        folder,
+        train_batch_size=16,
+        gradient_accumulate_every=1,
+        train_num_steps=1,
+        save_and_sample_every=100,
+        num_samples=1,
+        augment_horizontal_flip=False,
+        results_folder=results_folder,
+        calculate_fid=calculate_fid,
+        num_fid_samples=128,
+    )
+
+
+def create_images(folder):
+    folder.mkdir()
+    for index in range(100):
+        pixels = np.full((8, 8), index + 1, dtype=np.uint8)
+        Image.fromarray(pixels).save(folder / f"{index:03d}.png")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["denoising_diffusion_pytorch", "repaint"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("calculate_fid", [False, True])
+def test_real_statistics_do_not_advance_training(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch, variant, calculate_fid
+):
+    module = importlib.import_module(f"denoising_diffusion_pytorch.{variant}")
+    original_cycle = module.cycle
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        module, "cycle", lambda loader: CountedIterator(original_cycle(loader))
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "cpu_count", lambda: 0)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(fid_evaluation, "InceptionV3", DeterministicInception)
+    folder = tmp_path / "images"
+    create_images(folder)
+    trainer = make_trainer(module, folder, tmp_path / "results", calculate_fid)
+    trainer.train()
+    assert trainer.step == 1
+    assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 1
+    before = next(trainer.model.parameters()).detach().clone()
+
+    if calculate_fid:
+        trainer.fid_scorer.load_or_precalc_dataset_stats()
+        assert trainer.fid_scorer.dataset_stats_loaded
+        assert np.isfinite(trainer.fid_scorer.m2).all()
+        assert np.isfinite(trainer.fid_scorer.s2).all()
+        assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 1, "FID consumed the training iterator"
+
+    trainer.train_num_steps = 2
+    trainer.train()
+    assert trainer.step == 2
+    assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 2
+    assert not torch.equal(before, next(trainer.model.parameters()))
+
+
+def distributed_worker(rank, port, folder, results_folder, variant):
+    os.environ.update(
+        MASTER_ADDR="127.0.0.1",
+        MASTER_PORT=str(port),
+        RANK=str(rank),
+        LOCAL_RANK=str(rank),
+        WORLD_SIZE="2",
+        ACCELERATE_USE_CPU="true",
+    )
+    torch.set_num_threads(1)
+    distributed.init_process_group(
+        "gloo", rank=rank, world_size=2, timeout=timedelta(seconds=15)
+    )
+    phase_path = results_folder.parent / f"rank-{rank}.json"
+
+    def record_phase(phase):
+        phase_path.write_text(json.dumps({"rank": rank, "phase": phase}))
+
+    record_phase("initialized")
+    try:
+        module = prepare_module(variant)
+        trainer = make_trainer(module, folder, results_folder, calculate_fid=True)
+        trainer.train()
+        assert trainer.step == 1
+        assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 1
+        record_phase("first_training_step_complete")
+
+        # The first training epoch has fewer than eight batches on each rank.
+        # Rank zero must compute its 128-image statistics without a collective.
+        if rank == 0:
+            record_phase("collecting_real_statistics")
+            trainer.fid_scorer.load_or_precalc_dataset_stats()
+            assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 1, "FID consumed the training iterator"
+            assert np.isfinite(trainer.fid_scorer.m2).all()
+            assert np.isfinite(trainer.fid_scorer.s2).all()
+        record_phase("waiting_for_real_statistics")
+        distributed.barrier()
+
+        before = next(trainer.model.parameters()).detach().clone()
+        trainer.train_num_steps = 2
+        trainer.train()
+        assert trainer.step == 2
+        assert trainer.dl.next_calls == 2
+        assert not torch.equal(before, next(trainer.model.parameters()))
+        weights = torch.cat(
+            [parameter.detach().reshape(-1) for parameter in trainer.model.parameters()]
+        )
+        assert torch.isfinite(weights).all()
+        replicas = [torch.empty_like(weights) for _ in range(2)]
+        distributed.all_gather(replicas, weights)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(replicas[0], replicas[1], rtol=0, atol=0)
+        record_phase("second_training_step_and_gradient_sync_complete")
+    finally:
+        distributed.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["denoising_diffusion_pytorch", "repaint"])
+def test_rank_zero_statistics_leave_distributed_training_synchronized(
+    tmp_path, variant
+):
+    folder = tmp_path / "images"
+    create_images(folder)
+    with socket.socket() as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+    multiprocessing.spawn(
+        distributed_worker,
+        args=(port, folder, tmp_path / "results", variant),
+        nprocs=2,
+        join=True,
+    )

+from typing import ClassVar
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import fid_evaluation
+
+
+class SmallFeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
+    BLOCK_INDEX_BY_DIM: ClassVar[dict] = {3: 0}
+
+    def __init__(self, blocks):
+        super().__init__()
+
+    def forward(self, samples):
+        return [samples.mean(dim=(-1, -2), keepdim=True)]
+
+
+class Sampler(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, fail=False):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.norm = nn.BatchNorm2d(3)
+        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.5)
+        self.fail = fail
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def sample(self, batch_size):
+        self.calls.append([module.training for module in self.modules()])
+        if self.fail and len(self.calls) == 2:
+            raise RuntimeError("sampling failed")
+        return self.dropout(self.norm(torch.randn(batch_size, 3, 4, 4)))
+
+
+def make_evaluator(monkeypatch, tmp_path, sampler):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(fid_evaluation, "InceptionV3", SmallFeatureExtractor)
+    real = iter([torch.randn(2, 3, 4, 4), torch.randn(2, 3, 4, 4)])
+    return fid_evaluation.FIDEvaluation(
+        batch_size=2, dl=real, sampler=sampler, channels=3, stats_dir=tmp_path,
+        device="cpu", num_fid_samples=4, inception_block_idx=3,
+    )
+
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fail", [False, True])
+def test_fid_restores_every_sampler_module_mode(monkeypatch, tmp_path, mode, fail):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    sampler = Sampler(fail=fail)
+    sampler.train(mode != "eval")
+    if mode == "frozen_norm":
+        sampler.norm.eval()
+    before = [module.training for module in sampler.modules()]
+    evaluator = make_evaluator(monkeypatch, tmp_path, sampler)
+
+    if fail:

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch import ElucidatedDiffusion, Unet
+
+
+def make_diffusion(steps):
+    torch.manual_seed(16)
+    model = Unet(
+        dim=8, dim_mults=(1, 2), channels=1, attn_heads=1,
+        attn_dim_head=8, learned_sinusoidal_cond=True,
+    )
+    return ElucidatedDiffusion(
+        model, image_size=8, channels=1, num_sample_steps=steps,
+        sigma_min=0.002, sigma_max=2.0, S_churn=0,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("steps", [1, 2, 5, 32])
+def test_schedule_is_finite_and_keeps_sampling_endpoints(steps):
+    diffusion = make_diffusion(steps)
+
+    schedule = diffusion.sample_schedule()
+
+    assert schedule.shape == (steps + 1,)
+    assert torch.isfinite(schedule).all()
+    assert (schedule[:-1] > schedule[1:]).all()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(schedule[0], torch.tensor(diffusion.sigma_max))
+    assert schedule[-1] == 0
+    if steps > 1:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(schedule[-2], torch.tensor(diffusion.sigma_min))
+        positions = torch.linspace(0, 1, steps)
+        expected = (
+            diffusion.sigma_max ** (1 / diffusion.rho)
+            + positions * (diffusion.sigma_min ** (1 / diffusion.rho) - diffusion.sigma_max ** (1 / diffusion.rho))
+        ) ** diffusion.rho
+        torch.testing.assert_close(schedule[:-1], expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["sample", "sample_using_dpmpp"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("override", [False, True])
+def test_single_step_native_unet_matches_terminal_denoising(method, override):
+    diffusion = make_diffusion(32 if override else 1)
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    initial_noise = diffusion.sigma_max * torch.randn(2, 1, 8, 8)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        expected = diffusion.preconditioned_network_forward(
+            initial_noise, diffusion.sigma_max, clamp=method == "sample"
+        ).clamp(-1, 1) * 0.5 + 0.5
+    calls = []
+    handle = diffusion.net.register_forward_hook(lambda _module, _inputs, output: calls.append(output.shape))
+    kwargs = {"num_sample_steps": 1} if override else {}
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+        actual = getattr(diffusion, method)(batch_size=2, **kwargs)
+    finally:
+        handle.remove()
+
+    assert calls == [torch.Size([2, 1, 8, 8])]
+    assert torch.isfinite(actual).all()

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["sample", "sample_using_dpmpp", "sample_schedule"])

+    diffusion = make_diffusion(32)

+def test_rmsnorm_matches_channel_rms_values_and_gradients(shape, dtype):
+    x = torch.linspace(-2., 3., torch.tensor(shape).prod().item(), dtype = dtype)
+    x = x.reshape(shape).requires_grad_(True)
+    norm = RMSNorm(shape[1]).to(dtype = dtype)

+        norm.g.copy_(torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, shape[1], dtype = dtype).reshape_as(norm.g))
+
+    actual = norm(x)
+    expected = x / x.square().mean(dim = 1, keepdim = True).sqrt() * norm.g
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+
+    weights = torch.linspace(-1., 1., x.numel(), dtype = dtype).reshape_as(x)
+    actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad((actual * weights).sum(), (x, norm.g))
+    expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad((expected * weights).sum(), (x, norm.g))
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_grads, expected_grads):

+"""Loss targets must follow the permutation actually used to corrupt each image."""
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment
+from denoising_diffusion_pytorch.denoising_diffusion_pytorch import GaussianDiffusion, extract
+
+
+class ExactTarget(nn.Module):
+    channels = out_dim = 1
+    self_condition = False
+
+    def __init__(self, clean, objective):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.clean = clean
+        self.objective = objective
+        self.error = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros_like(clean))
+        self.seen = []
+
+    def forward(self, x, t, x_self_cond=None):
+        self.seen.append(x.detach().clone())
+        alpha = extract(self.alpha, t, x.shape)
+        sigma = extract(self.sigma, t, x.shape)
+        noise = (x - alpha * self.clean) / sigma
+        target = {"pred_noise": noise, "pred_x0": self.clean,
+                  "pred_v": alpha * noise - sigma * self.clean}[self.objective]
+        return target + self.error
+
+
+def build(objective, immiscible=True, minimum_snr=False):
+    clean = torch.tensor([-0.75, 0.75]).reshape(2, 1, 1, 1).expand(2, 1, 4, 4).clone()
+    noise = torch.tensor([0.25, -0.25]).reshape(2, 1, 1, 1).expand_as(clean).clone()
+    model = ExactTarget(clean, objective)
+    diffusion = GaussianDiffusion(model, image_size=4, timesteps=8, beta_schedule="cosine",
+                                  objective=objective, immiscible=immiscible,
+                                  min_snr_loss_weight=minimum_snr)
+    model.alpha, model.sigma = diffusion.sqrt_alphas_cumprod, diffusion.sqrt_one_minus_alphas_cumprod
+    return diffusion, clean, noise, torch.tensor([2, 5])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("objective", ["pred_noise", "pred_x0", "pred_v"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("minimum_snr", [False, True])
+def test_perfect_assigned_target_has_zero_loss_and_gradient(objective, minimum_snr):
+    diffusion, clean, noise, times = build(objective, minimum_snr=minimum_snr)
+    expected_order = linear_sum_assignment(torch.cdist(clean.flatten(1), noise.flatten(1)).numpy())[1]
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(expected_order, [1, 0])
+    losses = diffusion((clean + 1) / 2, times=times, noise=noise.clone(), loss_reduction="none")
+    assert losses.shape == (2,)
+    assert losses.max().item() < 1e-10

+from copy import deepcopy
+import importlib
+
+import pytest
